_about: Operator running many agents unattended. All seven material facets scored -- the only segment on the board with no unrun cells, which is not a coincidence: this is the shape fak was built for, so it is the shape that got measured.

fak.source: BENCHMARK-AUTHORITY.md headline row, `headline-qwen-50x5.json` (50 turns x 5 agents): fak does 1 unit of prefill work where naive re-prefill does 60.3, eliminating 1 - 1/60.3 = 0.983

alt.source: the tuned arm of the same artifact: 4.1 units of 60.3, eliminating 0.932

basis: docs/serve-config.md 3,286 w + AGENTS.md 10,166 w -- the read to a configured `fak serve` fronting a shared endpoint
wiring an existing worker pool through the endpoint

cells.note: The 5-agent measurement matches this buyer's shape exactly: the reuse being measured is CROSS-agent prefix sharing, which is the thing a fleet has and a single developer does not. This is the one segment where the headline number is quoted in its native regime.
cells.fence: Measured on Qwen2.5-1.5B Q8_0 on a single host. Radix prefix reuse is scale-free in principle; this ratio is not measured at frontier scale or against a production multi-tenant cache. The related RadixAttention row records an 86.7% hit rate, which is 100% of optimal on that corpus -- the mechanism is at its ceiling, the workload is not the buyer's.

fak.source: tools/loopgate `verified-vs-naive-loop.report.json`: the governed arm cuts false-done from 0.50 to 0.00 (net +3,900 tokens), with one-holder leases and runaway/injection caps; the ungoverned arm does none of it

alt.source: the ungoverned arm of the same report: false-done 0.50

basis: POLICY.md 1,726 w + docs/governed-agent-quickstart.md 1,361 w, plus wiring leases into an existing worker pool

cells.note: This is the reason this buyer exists as a segment. Half of unattended runs falsely reporting success is the operator's actual daily problem, and it is the one axis where the mechanism reaches the definitional ceiling. It is also where the claim cap bites hardest: the raw arithmetic puts this cell near the top of the ladder and the MODELED cap pulls it back to CRUISE, because the corpus is authored. That gap between what the arithmetic says and what the evidence supports is the highest-value benchmark work in the repo.
cells.fence: The 0.50 baseline comes from an AUTHORED corpus in tools/loopgate, not from field measurement of a real fleet. The governing mechanism (leases, caps, external verification) is real and tested; the rate it is scored against is constructed. Capped at CRUISE for that reason -- a simulated corpus cannot buy a category-defining claim.

fak.source: `compaction_budget=48000` in `docs/nightrun/cache-savings.jsonl` -- the resident context a session is held to -- against a 200,000-token window

alt.source: definitional: an unmanaged client holds the whole history, so it needs the whole window and then stops

basis: compaction is on by default once the guard is running; no configuration beyond the serve setup

cells.fence: Scores the enforced resident budget, not work preserved across a compaction fire. For unattended runs the second is what matters and it is unmeasured.

fak.source: BENCHMARK-AUTHORITY.md gateway row, `experiments/qwen36/gpu-server-r4-20260622/compare.json`: fak-gateway 1085.6 tok/s vs raw-SGLang 1451.6 at C=64 = 0.75x

alt.source: the raw-SGLang arm of the same comparison

basis: same serve configuration as the token-economy cell

cells.note: Quoted at the worst measured point. This buyer in particular should read the convergence: the same row records the tax falling to ~3% at saturation (C=128, 0.97x), and a fleet operator runs saturated by definition. The conservative number is scored; the realistic one is better.

fak.source: the session journal records the consequential decision classes -- model traffic, cache reuse, compaction, tool-policy verdicts, recovery -- post-hoc with no live attach. Scored 4 of 5, not 5 of 5: all five classes are RECORDED, but not in one artifact -- the session journal, `docs/nightrun/cache-savings.jsonl`, and the /metrics split are separate surfaces, so a full reconstruction means joining across them. Everything is captured; single-artifact reconstruction is not.

alt.source: OTel GenAI conventions instrument the model call and partially the cache; no span exists for a compaction, a tool verdict, or a recovery decision. 2 of 5 classes

basis: fak: journal on by default with the serve setup
alternative: a tracing stack across a fleet, which many operators already run

cells.note: For unattended fleets this compounds with run-integrity: knowing a run lied is only useful if you can then reconstruct where it started lying, and the tracing alternative carries no span for the verdict that would tell you.
cells.fence: Capability decomposition, not a benchmark; capped at RELATIVISTIC by the OBSERVED provenance rule.

fak.source: BENCHMARK-AUTHORITY.md AgentDojo row: full-stack ASR 0/38 = 0.000 versus 29/38 = 0.763 detection-only

alt.source: CaMeL ASR 0, MELON 0.0-2.4% -- already at the definitional floor

basis: fak: POLICY.md 1,726 w plus wiring existing workers behind the guard, no change to their data flow
alternative: restructuring every worker's data flow so untrusted content cannot reach the control path, across a fleet

cells.note: Parity on the number; the score comes entirely from the fact that restructuring a whole fleet costs three times what wrapping it does.
cells.fence: Benign and under-attack utility on the same suite is NEEDS_KEY. ASR 0 bounds harm without showing the workers still do their job.
